config.title: font-size and line-height

intro.title: font-size and line-height
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage to style text using CSS properties. You will learn the core concepts of controlling text size with 'font-size' and adjusting the spacing between lines of text with 'line-height'. The main technologies involved are CSS selectors and property-value pairs. By the end, you'll understand how these properties work together to improve readability and visual appeal. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to essential typography styling in web development.
intro.usecase: Controlling font-size and line-height is essential for creating readable, accessible interfaces across all web applications. In dashboards and data tables, proper text spacing ensures users can quickly scan metrics and reports without eye strain. Form interfaces rely on balanced typography to make labels, inputs, and error messages clear and scannable. Blog platforms and content management systems use these properties to create comfortable reading experiences with optimal paragraph spacing. Even in navigation menus and modals, consistent text sizing and line spacing contribute to professional, polished UI design.

objectives: Apply the font-size property to modify text dimensions in CSS.
Configure the line-height property to adjust vertical spacing between lines of text.
Implement relative and absolute units for font-size values.
Construct CSS rules that combine font-size and line-height for typographic control.
Manipulate line-height using unitless, percentage, and length values.
Update existing styles to improve readability through font-size and line-height adjustments.
Integrate font-size and line-height declarations within class and element selectors.

steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up the base HTML structure
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a basic structure including a heading, paragraph, and a container div. We'll style these elements with CSS in later steps.
steps.hint: Start with the standard HTML5 doctype, then add html, head, and body tags. Inside the body, include an h1, a p, and a div with class 'container'.
steps.analogousExample:
Main Heading

A paragraph of text.

Content goes here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a complete HTML file with the basic structure that we can style with CSS properties like font-size and line-height.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a heading (h1), a paragraph (p), and a div with class 'container' inside the body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all three required elements: an h1 heading, a paragraph, and a div with class='container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a complete HTML file with doctype, html, head, and body tags. Inside the body, include an h1, a p, and a div with class 'container'.

steps.title: Link the CSS file and add initial body styling
steps.instruction: Add a <link> element inside the <head> to connect a CSS file named 'styles.css',
steps.hint: The <link> element should have rel='stylesheet' and href='styles.css'. In the <style> tag, set font-family to a common web-safe font like 'Arial, sans-serif' and margin to 0.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Linking CSS and adding basic styles -->
<head>
    <title>My Page</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
    <style>
        body {
            font-family: 'Georgia, serif';
            margin: 20px;
        }
    </style>
</head>

steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML file will be linked to a CSS file and have basic body styling applied.
successCriteria: A <link> element with correct attributes connects to 'styles.css', and a <style> tag sets body font-family and margin.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added both the <link> for 'styles.css' and the <style> tag with body styles.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the structure: the <link> should be inside <head> with rel='stylesheet' and href='styles.css', and the <style> tag should contain body { font-family: ...; margin: ...; }.

steps.title: Apply font-size to the main heading
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to style the h1 element with a font-size of 36 pixels.
steps.hint: In your CSS file, target the h1 element and set the font-size property to 36px.
steps.seedCode: Welcome to Typography Basics
steps.expectedOutcome: The main heading will have a larger, more prominent font size of 36 pixels.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a rule for h1 with font-size: 36px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the font-size is set to exactly 36px for the h1 element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 element should have a font-size property with a value of 36px. Check your CSS rule syntax.

steps.title: Apply font-size to subheadings with relative units
steps.instruction: In your CSS file, add styling for h2 and h3 elements. Set the font-size for h2 to 1.5rem and for h3 to 1.2em.
steps.hint: Use the selectors h2 and h3, then set font-size with the specified relative units.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will include font-size rules for h2 and h3 using rem and em units.
successCriteria: h2 has font-size: 1.5rem; and h3 has font-size: 1.2em; in the CSS.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure both h2 and h3 have font-size set with the correct units.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the h2 and h3 selectors and set their font-size properties correctly.

steps.title: Set font-size for paragraph text
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for paragraph elements to set their font-size to 1rem.
steps.hint: Target the p selector and use the font-size property with the value 1rem.
steps.expectedOutcome: Paragraph text will have a readable font-size of 1rem.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for p elements with font-size: 1rem is added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set a readable font-size for paragraph text.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a rule for p with font-size: 1rem.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph styling is missing or incorrect. Please add a CSS rule for p with font-size: 1rem.

steps.title: Add line-height to the main heading
steps.instruction: Add a line-height property to the existing h1 selector using a unitless value (like 1.5).
steps.hint: Inside the h1 rule, add line-height: 1.5; after the font-size property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h1 heading will have increased vertical spacing between lines, making it more readable.
successCriteria: The h1 selector includes a line-height property with a unitless value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added line-height, but make sure it's a unitless number (like 1.5) rather than a fixed unit like px or em.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 selector doesn't have a line-height property yet. Add line-height: 1.5; inside the h1 rule.

steps.title: Apply line-height to subheadings
steps.instruction: Add line-height declarations to the h2 and h3 elements in your CSS.
steps.hint: Look for the comment '/* Add your h2 and h3 styling here */' and add line-height properties to those selectors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The h2 and h3 elements will have line-height applied, improving vertical spacing.
successCriteria: Both h2 and h3 selectors have line-height properties with appropriate values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added line-height to one subheading, but both h2 and h3 need it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added line-height properties to both h2 and h3 selectors.

steps.title: Set line-height for paragraph text
steps.instruction: Add a line-height property to the paragraph styling to improve readability.
steps.hint: Use the line-height property with a unitless value (like 1.5) or a length value (like 1.5em).
steps.expectedOutcome: Paragraph text will have improved vertical spacing between lines.
successCriteria: The paragraph styling includes a line-height property with a valid value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a line-height property to the paragraph styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph styling doesn't include a line-height property. Add it to improve text spacing.

steps.title: Create a comparison section with different font-size and line-height values
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS class named '.comparison' and define two paragraph styles within it to demonstrate different typography combinations.
steps.hint: Create a class selector starting with a dot, then define two paragraph selectors inside it with different font-size and line-height values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS class '.comparison' is created with two paragraph styles showing different font-size and line-height combinations.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a '.comparison' class with at least two paragraph selectors inside, each with distinct font-size and line-height values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your '.comparison' class contains at least two paragraph styles with different font-size and line-height values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please create a CSS class named '.comparison' with two paragraph styles inside, each with different font-size and line-height values.

steps.title: Add responsive font-size using viewport units
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a .responsive-heading class that uses viewport width units (vw) for font-size to create responsive typography.
steps.hint: Use the vw unit to set font-size based on the viewport width. For example: font-size: 4vw;
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule for .responsive-heading with font-size using vw units will be added to the stylesheet.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a .responsive-heading selector with a font-size property using vw units.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the responsive heading rule, but check that you're using the vw unit correctly for the font-size property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The responsive heading rule is missing or doesn't use vw units for font-size. Try adding a .responsive-heading class with font-size: [number]vw;
